<problem>
Let \(X\) be a smooth connected complex projective curve of genus \(g\geq2\), and let \(K_X\) be its canonical line bundle. For an integer \(n\geq2\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb C\), a rank-\(n\), degree-zero \(\lambda\)-connection is a vector bundle \(V\) with a \(\mathbb C\)-linear operator \(D^\lambda:V\to V\otimes K_X\) satisfying \(D^\lambda(fs)=fD^\lambda(s)+\lambda s\otimes df\). It is semistable, respectively stable, if every proper nonzero subbundle \(F\subset V\) satisfying \(D^\lambda(F)\subset F\otimes K_X\) has degree at most zero, respectively strictly less than zero.

Let \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Hod}}(X,n)\) be the coarse moduli space of S-equivalence classes of these semistable objects, with \(\lambda\) varying and with no determinant fixed. Here S-equivalence at a fixed \(\lambda\) means that the direct sums of stable degree-zero factors obtained from filtrations by invariant subbundles are isomorphic. Write \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Dol}}(X,n)\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{dR}}(X,n)\) for its fibers at \(\lambda=0\) and \(\lambda=1\), respectively.

The action \(c\cdot(\lambda,V,D^\lambda)=(c\lambda,V,cD^\lambda)\) of \(\mathbb C^\times\) has a limit \(r(y)=\lim_{c\to0}c\cdot y\) for every coarse point \(y\), lying in the full fixed locus inside \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Dol}}(X,n)\). A stable full chain is a stable Higgs bundle \((\bigoplus_{i=1}^n L_i,\theta)\), where the \(L_i\) are line bundles of total degree zero and the only nonzero components of \(\theta\) are maps \(\theta_i:L_i\to L_{i+1}\otimes K_X\), each nonzero, for \(1\leq i<n\). Call a connected component \(P\) of the full fixed locus a stable full-chain component if every point of \(P\) represents a stable full chain. Components here are taken in the full fixed locus, not merely in its stable part.

For such a component and \(\star\in\{\mathrm{Hod},\mathrm{Dol},\mathrm{dR}\}\), define
\[
S_P^\star=\{y\in\mathcal M_\star(X,n):r(y)\in P\}.
\]
All loci are given their reduced structures, dimensions are complex algebraic dimensions, and closures are Zariski closures in the full indicated moduli space.

Define the rank-and-fiber incidence set
\[
\mathcal E_X=\left\{(n,\star)\in\mathbb Z_{\geq2}\times\{\mathrm{Hod},\mathrm{Dol},\mathrm{dR}\}:\begin{array}{l}
\text{there exist distinct stable full-chain components }P,Q\
\text{at rank }n\text{ such that }\dim S_P^\star=\dim S_Q^\star\text{ and}\
\varnothing\ne\overline{S_P^\star}\cap S_Q^\star\subsetneq S_Q^\star
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
Determine \(\mathcal E_X\) explicitly for every such curve \(X\).
</problem>

3	Put \(h=g-1\). The answer is independent of the curve, including its genus:
4	\[
5	\boxed{\displaystyle
6	\mathcal E_X=\{(n,\star):n\geq4,\quad
7	\star\in\{\mathrm{Hod},\mathrm{Dol},\mathrm{dR}\}\}.}
8	\]
9	
10	An important point in the proof is that an incidence in the Dolbeault fiber does not, by itself, imply an incidence in the de Rham fiber. We prove the latter using a deformation calculation.
11	
12	## 1. Full-chain components and their dimensions
13	
14	Write \(d_i=\deg L_i\), and put
15	\[
16	m_i=2h+d_{i+1}-d_i.
17	\]
18	A degree vector \(d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) occurs for a stable full chain precisely when
19	\[
20	\sum_i d_i=0,\qquad m_i\geq0,\qquad
21	\sum_{i=1}^j d_i>0\quad(1\leq j<n).                    \tag{1}
22	\]
23	Indeed, over the function field a full chain is a single nilpotent Jordan block. Its invariant subspaces are the tails. Thus stability is exactly the last set of inequalities.
24	
25	For a vector satisfying (1), the corresponding fixed locus is
26	\[
27	P_d\cong
28	\operatorname{Pic}^{d_1}(X)\times
29	\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}\operatorname{Sym}^{m_i}(X).           \tag{2}
30	\]
31	Explicitly, choose \(L_1\) and effective divisors \(D_i\) of degrees \(m_i\), and set
32	\[
33	L_{i+1}=L_iK_X^{-1}(D_i).
34	\]
35	The nonzero maps are then determined up to the automorphisms of the line bundles.
36	
37	In particular, \(P_d\) is connected and proper, and
38	\[
39	\dim P_d=g+\sum_i m_i
40	       =g+2h(n-1)+d_n-d_1.                            \tag{3}
41	\]
42	It is a component of the **full** fixed locus. To justify this last assertion, in the stable fixed locus the ranks and weights of the Hodge decomposition are locally constant. Consequently, (2) is open there. It is also proper, hence closed in the full fixed locus. Since the stable locus is open, it is open and closed in the full fixed locus.
43	
44	Let
45	\[
46	N=n^2h+1.
47	\]
48	The standard attracting-set dimension formulas are
49	\[
50	\begin{aligned}
51	\dim S_{P_d}^{\mathrm{Dol}}
52	 &=N+\dim P_d,\\
53	\dim S_{P_d}^{\mathrm{dR}}
54	 &=N+\dim P_d,\\
55	\dim S_{P_d}^{\mathrm{Hod}}
56	 &=N+\dim P_d+1.                                     \tag{4}
57	\end{aligned}
58	\]
59	Here all three attracting sets are irreducible.
60	
61	For completeness, these statements follow from the smooth stable locus and the Białynicki–Birula theorem. An object with stable limit is itself stable. The Dolbeault tangent space has dimension \(2N\), and its symplectic form has weight one. The tangent weights pair as \(w,1-w\), so there are exactly \(N\) positive weights. In Hodge moduli there is one additional positive direction, namely \(\lambda\), of weight one. On an attracting affine fiber, \(\lambda\) is a nonzero linear coordinate among the weight-one coordinates. Its fibers therefore have the asserted dimensions and are irreducible.
62	
63	It follows from (3)–(4) that
64	\[
65	\dim S_{P_d}^{\star}=\dim S_{P_e}^{\star}
66	\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
67	d_1-d_n=e_1-e_n.                                    \tag{5}
68	\]
69	
70	We will also use the following elementary observation.
71	
72	**Equal-dimension observation.** If two distinct irreducible locally closed sets have the same dimension, neither can be contained in the closure of the other.
73	
74	Otherwise their closures would be the same irreducible variety, and the two locally closed sets would contain disjoint dense open subsets of that variety. Thus, in our constructions, once a nonempty incidence is established, its being proper follows automatically.
75	
76	## 2. Why ranks two and three are excluded
77	
78	We recall the weight test for attracting sets.
79	
80	**Weight test.** Let a quasiprojective variety have a linearized ample line bundle, and let \(P,Q\) be distinct proper fixed components. If the line bundle has the same weight on \(P\) and \(Q\), then
81	\[
82	\overline{S_P}\cap S_Q=\varnothing.                  \tag{6}
83	\]
84	
85	To see this, take an equivariant projective embedding given by a power of the line bundle. Points attracted to \(P\) have a specified lowest nonzero weight coordinate. On the open set where this weight coordinate is nonzero, projection to its weight space sends \(S_P\) to \(P\). Since \(P\) is proper, the same holds on its closure. A point attracted to a different component of the same weight cannot belong to that closure.
86	
87	For Hodge moduli, the determinant-of-cohomology GIT polarization has, at a full chain, weight
88	\[
89	A+B\sum_{i=1}^n(i-1)d_i,\qquad B\ne0,               \tag{7}
90	\]
91	where \(A,B\) do not depend on \(d\). One can calculate this directly using a scalar-invariant determinant line
92	\[
93	\bigl(\det R\Gamma(V\otimes A_0)\bigr)^{\otimes n}
94	\otimes
95	(\det V_x)^{-\chi(V\otimes A_0)}.
96	\]
97	Give \(L_i\) weight \(i-1\). The terms involving \(\deg A_0+1-g\) cancel, leaving
98	\(n\sum(i-1)d_i\), up to the choice of the ample dual and a positive power. This is the usual determinant polarization in the Quot construction, also for the family of \(\lambda\)-connections.
99	
100	In rank two, equality in (5) determines the entire degree vector. By (2), there cannot be distinct components of that degree vector.
101	
102	In rank three,
103	\[
104	2d_1+d_2=d_1-d_3,
105	\]
106	so equality in (5) implies equality of the weights in (7). The weight test excludes incidence in Hodge moduli.
107	
108	It also excludes incidence in either fiber: a fiberwise closure is contained in the closure in Hodge moduli. We have proved
109	\[
110	(n,\star)\notin\mathcal E_X\qquad(n=2,3).             \tag{8}
111	\]
112	
113	## 3. The components used in every rank at least four
114	
115	Fix \(n\geq4\), and take
116	\[
117	q=(1,1,\underbrace{0,\ldots,0}_{n-4},-1,-1).
118	\]
119	Set
120	\[
121	p=q-e_2+e_3.                                       \tag{9}
122	\]
123	Both vectors satisfy (1). Only the second prefix sum changes, from two to one.
124	
125	Their arrow degrees satisfy
126	\[
127	m(p)=m(q)+(-1,2,-1,0,\ldots,0).                     \tag{10}
128	\]
129	The first and third entries of \(m(q)\) are positive. In particular, the right side is nonnegative. The endpoints in (9) are unchanged, so
130	\[
131	\dim S_{P_p}^{\star}=\dim S_{P_q}^{\star}
132	\quad\text{for all three }\star.                    \tag{11}
133	\]
134	
135	Choose a point \(x\in X\). We choose a chain in \(P_q\) with these extra properties:
136	\[
137	\begin{array}{ll}
138	\theta_1\text{ vanishes simply at }x,&
139	L_2L_1^{-1}\not\cong\mathcal O_X,\\
140	\theta_2(x)\ne0,&
141	\theta_3\text{ vanishes simply at }x.               \tag{12}
142	\end{array}
143	\]
144	These choices are possible on every curve in the question.
145	
146	Indeed, \(m_1(q)=2h\). Choose an effective divisor \(D_1\) of degree \(2h\), containing \(x\) simply, such that
147	\[
148	\mathcal O_X(D_1)\not\cong K_X.
149	\]
150	Such divisors exist because the Abel map on divisors containing \(x\) is not constant. Then
151	\[
152	L_2L_1^{-1}=K_X^{-1}(D_1)
153	\]
154	is a nontrivial degree-zero line bundle. Choose \(D_2\) avoiding \(x\), and \(D_3\) containing \(x\) simply. Their required degrees are nonnegative, and the degree of \(D_3\) is positive. All remaining divisors are arbitrary.
155	
156	Denote this chain by \(Q_0\).
157	
158	## 4. The Dolbeault incidence
159	
160	Inside the bundle of \(Q_0\), replace \(L_2\) by \(L_2(-x)\). Call the resulting bundle \(W\), and denote its induced Higgs field by \(\phi\).
161	
162	The Higgs field preserves \(W\), by the first condition in (12). Locally at \(x\), the second and third arrows of \(W\) vanish. Thus \(\phi(x)\) is zero on the plane
163	\[
164	U=L_2(-x)_x\oplus L_{3,x}.
165	\]
166	For each line \(\ell\subset U\), take the upper elementary modification
167	\[
168	W\subset E_\ell\subset W(x),\qquad E_\ell/W=\ell.
169	\]
170	Because \(\phi(x)\ell=0\), the Higgs field extends holomorphically to \(E_\ell\).
171	
172	Let \(e_2,e_3\) be bases for the two summands of \(U\), and put
173	\[
174	\ell_t=\mathbb C(e_2+t e_3).
175	\]
176	For \(t=0\), the modified Higgs bundle is \(Q_0\). For \(t\ne0\), the natural saturated full filtration has degree vector \(p\). Its graded arrow divisors are
177	\[
178	D_1-x,\qquad D_2+2x,\qquad D_3-x,\qquad D_4,\ldots.
179	\]
180	They are all effective and all arrows are nonzero. Its associated graded is therefore a stable full chain in \(P_p\). Consequently,
181	\[
182	(E_{\ell_t},\phi)\in S_{P_p}^{\mathrm{Dol}}\quad(t\ne0),
183	\qquad
184	(E_{\ell_0},\phi)=Q_0\in P_q.
185	\]
186	Hence
187	\[
188	Q_0\in
189	\overline{S_{P_p}^{\mathrm{Dol}}}\cap S_{P_q}^{\mathrm{Dol}}.       \tag{13}
190	\]
191	
192	The same point gives an incidence in Hodge moduli. Together with (11) and the equal-dimension observation, this proves the required statement for \(\mathrm{Dol}\) and \(\mathrm{Hod}\).
193	
194	## 5. Deforming the incidence to nonzero \(\lambda\)
195	
196	Here is the deformation calculation needed for the de Rham fiber.
197	
198	### 5.1 Local equations
199	
200	Use a coordinate \(z\) at \(x\) and a flag-compatible frame of \(W\), fixed modulo \(z^2\). On the plane with basis \(e_2,e_3\), write
201	\[
202	\ell_t=\mathbb C(e_2+t e_3).
203	\]
204	Consider logarithmic \(\lambda\)-connections on \(W\), with residue
205	\[
206	R_{\lambda,t}
207	=\lambda(e_2+t e_3)e_2^*.                            \tag{14}
208	\]
209	Thus
210	\[
211	R_{\lambda,t}^2=\lambda R_{\lambda,t},\qquad
212	\operatorname{tr}R_{\lambda,t}=\lambda,\qquad
213	R_{\lambda,t}\ell_t=\lambda\ell_t.
214	\]
215	
216	Require the following:
217	
218	* the connection matrix is upper Hessenberg, i.e. it satisfies Griffiths transversality for the full filtration of \(W\);
219	* its third subdiagonal symbol vanishes at \(x\);
220	* if its local matrix is
221	  \[
222	  \lambda d+\left(\frac{R_{\lambda,t}}z+M_0+O(z)\right)dz,
223	  \]
224	  then
225	  \[
226	  M_0\ell_t\subset\ell_t.                           \tag{15}
227	  \]
228	
229	These are algebraic conditions. More explicitly, the restrictions on \(M_0\) are
230	\[
231	(M_0)_{43}=0,\quad
232	(M_0)_{12}+t(M_0)_{13}=0,
233	\]
234	\[
235	(M_0)_{32}+t(M_0)_{33}
236	-t(M_0)_{22}-t^2(M_0)_{23}=0.                       \tag{16}
237	\]
238	Their ranks are constant near \(t=0\).
239	
240	Conditions (14)–(15) say exactly that the connection extends holomorphically to the upper modification \(E_{\ell_t}\). Indeed, in the modified lattice the additional generator is \((e_2+t e_3)/z\). Its double pole cancels because \(R_{\lambda,t}\ell_t=\lambda\ell_t\), and its remaining complementary simple pole vanishes precisely by (15).
241	
242	The vanishing of the third symbol ensures Griffiths transversality for the induced filtrations on \(E_{\ell_t}\).
243	
244	### 5.2 The obstruction group
245	
246	We verify that the above local conditions admit simultaneous global deformations in \(\lambda\) and \(t\).
247	
248	The auxiliary Higgs bundle \((W,\phi)\) has degree \(-1\) and is stable. Its invariant tails have negative integral degrees, so their slopes are strictly below \(-1/n\).
249	
250	Write \(W=\bigoplus M_i\), where
251	\[
252	M_2=L_2(-x),\qquad M_i=L_i\quad(i\ne2).
253	\]
254	Let \(\mathcal A\) be the sheaf of upper-triangular endomorphisms. With the frame fixed modulo \(z^2\), the infinitesimal automorphism sheaf is
255	\[
256	\mathcal A(-2x).
257	\]
258	At \((\lambda,t)=(0,0)\), the homogeneous connection variations form the sheaf \(\mathcal B\) of upper-Hessenberg \(K_X\)-valued matrices, with the additional requirements that the entries
259	\[
260	(1,2),\quad(3,2),\quad(4,3)                          \tag{17}
261	\]
262	vanish at \(x\).
263	
264	The deformation complex is therefore
265	\[
266	\mathcal C^\bullet:
267	\mathcal A(-2x)\xrightarrow{[\phi,\;]}
268	\mathcal B.                                         \tag{18}
269	\]
270	As usual, a Čech lifting calculation places the obstruction to extending a deformation across a square-zero thickening in
271	\(\mathbb H^2(\mathcal C^\bullet)\). The local conditions themselves are unobstructed because (16) has constant rank.
272	
273	We claim
274	\[
275	\mathbb H^2(\mathcal C^\bullet)\cong\mathbb C,
276	\quad\text{and trace induces this isomorphism}.       \tag{19}
277	\]
278	
279	Here are the details. By Serre duality, a dual obstruction is represented by a section \(f\) of \(\mathcal B^*\otimes K_X\), with the commutator condition dual to (18).
280	
281	For ordinary upper-Hessenberg matrices, such an \(f\) is represented by a lower-triangular matrix together with its first upper diagonal. The three conditions (17) additionally permit simple poles in the transposed positions
282	\[
283	(2,1),\quad(2,3),\quad(3,4).
284	\]
285	The first of these cannot occur:
286	\[
287	H^0\!\left(\operatorname{Hom}(M_1,M_2)(x)\right)
288	=
289	H^0(L_2L_1^{-1})=0                                 \tag{20}
290	\]
291	by (12).
292	
293	Let \(f_i\) denote the entries on the first upper diagonal and let \(\phi_i\) be the nonzero subdiagonal arrows of \(\phi\). The diagonal commutator equations are, successively,
294	\[
295	\phi_1f_1=0,\quad
296	\phi_2f_2-\phi_1f_1=0,\quad\ldots,\quad
297	-\phi_{n-1}f_{n-1}=0.
298	\]
299	Thus all \(f_i\) vanish, including the permitted meromorphic ones. What remains is an actual holomorphic lower-triangular endomorphism commuting with \(\phi\). Stability of \((W,\phi)\) makes it scalar. Conversely, scalar endomorphisms give the trace obstruction. This proves (19). Fixing the determinant and determinant connection removes it.
300	
301	There is no determinant obstruction to the prescribed residues: \(\deg W=-1\), and
302	\(\operatorname{tr}R_{\lambda,t}=\lambda\). A line bundle of degree \(-1\) has a logarithmic connection with one residue \(1\); multiplying by \(\lambda\) supplies the required determinant \(\lambda\)-connection. This is the degree–residue criterion.
303	
304	We conclude that the moduli problem defined by (14)–(16), with fixed determinant connection, is smooth over the \((\lambda,t)\)-plane at our point.
305	
306	### 5.3 The resulting de Rham boundary
307	
308	On the axis \(\lambda=0\), the constant Higgs bundle \((W,\phi)\), with the varying lines \(\ell_t\), is already a family satisfying all the conditions. Smoothness extends it, étale locally, to a two-parameter algebraic family. One may see this directly by taking étale coordinates for a smooth morphism and extending the coordinates of the given section on \(\lambda=0\).
309	
310	Upper modification gives a family of holomorphic \(\lambda\)-connections on \(E_{\ell_t}\).
311	
312	* Along \(t=0\), its full filtration has degree vector \(q\).
313	* Along \(t\ne0\), it has degree vector \(p\).
314	* Nonvanishing of all graded arrows is open. It holds on the original Higgs family, and hence on the needed dense open part of the two-parameter family.
315	
316	Consequently, for a general nonzero value \(a\) of \(\lambda\), a point of \(S_{P_q}^{\lambda=a}\) is a limit, in that same fiber, of points of \(S_{P_p}^{\lambda=a}\). Scaling the connection by \(a^{-1}\) identifies this fiber with the de Rham fiber. Therefore
317	\[
318	\overline{S_{P_p}^{\mathrm{dR}}}
319	\cap S_{P_q}^{\mathrm{dR}}\ne\varnothing.              \tag{21}
320	\]
321	By (11) and irreducibility, this intersection is proper.
322	
323	This finishes the existence proof in every rank \(n\geq4\), in all three indicated moduli spaces.
324	
325	## 6. Python verification
326	
327	The geometric ingredients above are the Białynicki–Birula theorem, determinant-of-cohomology polarization, and deformation theory on a curve. The following code checks the algebraic calculations used in applying them:
328	
329	* the local residue and elementary-modification equations;
330	* the three exceptional entries in the dual obstruction calculation;
331	* the full rank of the diagonal commutator equations;
332	* the degree, stability, and dimension calculations;
333	* exhaustive low-rank degree-vector enumeration.
334	
335	I ran this code successfully. Finite enumeration is used only as a check, not as a substitute for the uniform proof.
336	
337	```python
338	import sympy as s
339	from collections import defaultdict
340	
341	# Rank-three identity and uniform degree-change identities.
342	h, a, b = s.symbols("h a b", integer=True)
343	d = [a, b, -a-b]
344	assert s.expand(2*d[0] + d[1] - (d[0]-d[2])) == 0
345	
346	n = s.symbols("n", integer=True, positive=True)
347	assert -1 + 2 - 1 == 0
348	assert s.expand((n-2) - (n-3)) == 1
349	
350	# Local residue and upper elementary modification.
351	z, t, lam = s.symbols("z t lam", nonzero=True)
352	r, u, v, w = s.symbols("r u v w")
353	ell = s.Matrix([1, t])
354	R = lam * ell * s.Matrix([[1, 0]])
355	
356	assert R*ell == lam*ell
357	assert R.trace() == lam
358	assert R*R == lam*R
359	
360	# M ell is in ell.
361	M = s.Matrix([[r, u], [t*r + t*t*u - t*w, w]])
362	assert s.det(s.Matrix.hstack(ell, M*ell)) == 0
